pr.title: Read a review's fetched head from its own ref, not FETCH_HEAD
pr.head: 5a9221cd5994dca5cb21606227a041c2a4d47be2

summary: When a review starts, project review setup fetches the pull request's head into the operator's checkout, the repository clone the review runs beside. It then confirms that the commit it fetched is the head SHA that GitHub reports, and refuses with the head moved when the two differ. project review move does the same when a review follows the head to a new commit.

Both commands read the fetched commit from FETCH_HEAD. Git rewrites that one file on every fetch in the checkout, so a fetch by another review, or by a summary publish, could land between the fetch and the read. setup then compared the wrong commit and refused, naming a SHA that was not on the pull request. A review loop running several reviews in one checkout hit this three times in one day.

This pull request makes each fetch write its commit to a ref that only this call uses, refs/projector/review-fetch/<pid>-<random>. The call reads the commit from that ref and deletes the ref. The check that the head moved keeps its meaning: it still compares the tip of the head branch, or of pull/<n>/head for a fork, with GitHub's SHA.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Operator checkout: the clone of the repository that a review runs beside. Several reviews can share it.
  • FETCH_HEAD: a file in .git/ where Git records what the latest fetch brought in. Every fetch rewrites it.
  • Temporary ref: refs/projector/review-fetch/<pid>-<random>, written by one fetch and deleted right after the read.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
One Projector review of 5a9221c found the head clean, with no finding threads. It ran a concurrency reproduction: at the base, 52 of 80 parallel fetches read the wrong commit or a half-written FETCH_HEAD, and at this head all 80 read the right commit.

One suggestion stands: the fetch still writes FETCH_HEAD, which nothing reads now.

groups.title: Each fetch reads its own ref
groups.kicker: The fix in the review fetch, its test, and the docs that describe it
intro: fetch in review.py is the one function that brings a commit into the operator checkout for a review. fetch_head calls it twice, once for the head and once for the base, and both setup and move call fetch_head.

The function now passes Git a refspec, +<ref>:refs/projector/review-fetch/<pid>-<random>, so the fetched commit lands in a ref named for this process and eight random hex digits. It reads that ref with rev-parse --verify <ref>^{commit}, and a finally block deletes the ref whether the read succeeds or fails. No other process writes that ref, so a concurrent fetch cannot change what the read returns.
The new test simulates the race by rewriting FETCH_HEAD to another commit right after every fetch, and checks that setup still succeeds and leaves no ref under refs/projector/.

checks.text: Concurrent fetches read the right commit. In a scratch clone, 8 worker processes ran fetch 80 times for two branches while another process kept fetching a third. At this head all 80 returned the right commit. With the base's fetch, 25 returned the other branch's commit and 27 failed on a half-written FETCH_HEAD. Neither run left a ref behind.
The full test suite passes at this head: 1080 tests with 1 skipped, under Python 3.12. project check and both claude plugin validate runs pass.

files.note: fetch writes the fetched commit to a temporary ref, reads it, and deletes the ref.

checks.text: The name joins the process ID with 32 random bits. The process ID is unique among live processes on one machine, and the random suffix separates two processes that share an ID across machines or PID namespaces. Nothing else in the repository reads or pushes refs/projector/review-fetch/.

The fetch still writes FETCH_HEAD, as it did before, so each review overwrites the operator's own FETCH_HEAD. Nothing reads it here any more. fetch_summaries in site/serve.py passes --no-write-fetch-head for the same reason, and the review suggested doing the same here.

The ref is deleted on every path that reaches the read. A KeyboardInterrupt raised during rev-parse still runs the deletion, and a fetch of a missing branch raises ReviewError without writing a ref. Both were run in a scratch clone.

files.note: A setup test that rewrites FETCH_HEAD after every fetch, as a concurrent fetch would.

checks.text: Run against the base's review.py, this test fails with the head moved to 7fcf168 while it was fetched. It passes at this head.
